programme.desc: Boston is a city of great historical and scientific importance.This is where prestigious universities such as Harvard and MIT are located, as well as the headquarters of Boston Dynamics, known for creating humanoid robots.Although the city is associated with the American Revolution, it also has lesser-known stories.Marcin will meet a guide who will talk about the first settlers and explain events such as the flooding of the city by molasses in the early 20th century, the smell of which can still be felt on hot days.Marcin will also talk to Walter Robinson from the Boston Globe about the famous journalistic investigation presented in the film "Spotlight", which revealed a scandal in the local archdiocese, affecting the city and the world.In addition, the host will take viewers to Salem, a town known for its witch trials from three hundred years ago.Today, the Salem witches attract tourists and are one of the area's main attractions.

programme.title: Secrets of the wrecks of the Baltic Sea
programme.desc: Franken is a German mechanically driven tanker sunk near Hel by Soviet aviation during World War II - on April 8, 1945.The wreck hides a story of great passion and, at the same time, great tragedy.Diving on it is demanding because you have to go below 40 meters, so partial decompression is necessary.In addition to the entire list of victims that Franken had when it sank in 1945, three divers should be added - a Czech and two Poles.The team places a symbolic expression of memory of the dead underwater, a monument that rests on the surface of one of the most dangerous wreck diving facilities.

programme.title: Secrets of the wrecks of the Baltic Sea
programme.desc: The controversial destruction of a historic ship which, against the will of the inhabitants of Rostock, Germany, was sold for scrap.Georg Büchner - a luxury liner lost buoyancy while being towed to the shipyard in Klaipeda, Lithuania, and went to the bottom.Former passenger Freddy Korthoudet tells us what an exclusive passenger ship the Büchner, once called the Charlesville, was.Tomek Stachura, together with a team of divers and a German journalist and enthusiast of the history of this machine, Merlin Franke, are trying to determine the actual course of events on May 30, 2013.It helps, among others:Frederik Janssens, Belgian souvenir collector.Divers descend to the wreck, which sank relatively recently and has not yet been destroyed by the sea.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: A series of reports presenting the customs and life situation of women living in distant corners of the globe.Journalist Martyna Wojciechowska once again sets out on risky expeditions to learn about the activities, passions and dreams of women living in different cultures.Stops in the third edition of the program include Samoa, Ghana and India.Together with her interlocutors, she experiences their joys and sorrows and participates in everyday activities.This allows her to understand contrasts and learn about different approaches to femininity in different parts of the world In the wastelands of Ghana, far from the settlements, there live women sentenced to banishment for crimes committed using witchcraft.Their guilt was confirmed by a simple ritual.Martyna Wojciechowska reaches one of the camps of women considered witches.They suffer from the loss of contact with their family and the rejection they experience because someone suspected them of dabbling in black magic.Among them are Amina and her granddaughter Rukaye, who after many years, thanks to the program's crew, get a chance to meet their loved ones.
